text:
maya: heads up — seeing a sudden surge of GPU nodes stuck NotReady in the europe-west2 preemptible pool, started ~10m ago. Pods are NoSchedule. Noticed device-plugin CrashLoopBackOff on affected nodes.

maya: kubectl get nodes | grep gpu-pool | tail -n 10
```
gpu-preempt-7x2k   NotReady   gpu,nvidia   3d   v1.28.4
gpu-preempt-9m1b   NotReady   gpu,nvidia   5d   v1.28.4
gpu-preempt-4c0r   Ready      gpu,nvidia   2h   v1.28.4
```

maya: device-plugin logs show discovery failure: 
```
I0403 12:08:10.123456 1 plugin.go:212] Starting device plugin
E0403 12:08:12.789012 1 plugin.go:298] failed to list devices: open /dev/nvidiactl: no such file or directory
panic: failed to discover GPUs: no devices found
```

gabe: ack, I'm oncall. Any kernel/driver updates rolled recently?

maya: not to my knowledge; node image didn't change. dmesg on one node shows a udev timing thing where modules come up after container runtime: 
```
[   10.345678] init: starting containerd
[   10.500123] systemd-udevd[432]: Process '/sbin/modprobe nvidia' failed with exit code 1
[   11.123456] nvidia: probe of 0000:03:00.0 failed with error -2
[   12.000000] nvidia: module loaded
[   12.100000] docker: starting
```

anika: looks like a race: kubelet/device-plugin startup path checks for /dev nodes before drivers are fully probed. If device-plugin starts too early it errors and kubelet marks node as GPU-Unhealthy => taints to NoSchedule.

infra-oncall: the quick mitigation is to restart nvidia-device-plugin daemonset on the nodes that recovered driver late. Can someone try drain/cordon -> restart plugin -> uncordon as a test on one node?

gabe: doing a test on gpu-preempt-7x2k now:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-preempt-7x2k
kubectl drain gpu-preempt-7x2k --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart daemonset/nvidia-device-plugin-daemonset
sleep 15
kubectl uncordon gpu-preempt-7x2k
```

gabe: update — after restart, plugin logs show devices enumerated and node turned Ready within ~30s.
```
I0403 12:14:20.987654 1 plugin.go:212] Starting device plugin
I0403 12:14:21.123456 1 plugin.go:256] Found 1 devices
```

maya: can we make this less manual? Seems like preemptible pool nodes are starting many pods concurrently and containerd ordering varies.

anika: two fixes we can evaluate: (1) ensure nvidia modules are loaded in early boot via cloud-init (modprobe in rc.local or systemd unit Before=kubelet.service), (2) update device-plugin to retry discovery with exponential backoff instead of panic (we saw the plugin exits on first failure).

infra-oncall: Also possible workaround: add a node boot probe script that waits for /dev/nvidia* before kubelet registers node. Might be heavy-handed.

gabe: I'll open a change to the node image to enable nvidia-persistenced and a systemd drop-in for ordering so nvidia-modprobe runs Before=kubelet. Patch in CI for canary.

maya: opened RFC: https://go/internal/rfcs/rdw-gpu-udev-startup (draft) — includes cloud-init + kubelet unit tweak + longer device-plugin retries.

anika: for immediate cluster-level mitigation we can add a DaemonSet init container that sleeps 10s before starting device-plugin on nodes with suspicious startup patterns. It's clunky but buys time.

infra-oncall: monitoring alert updated to include CrashLoopBackOff count for nvidia-device-plugin and total NotReady GPUs per pool. Will run rollout to 2 nodes in canary and report back in 30m. :eyes:

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0412-02 — GPU pool degradation europe-west2. Pager duty notified.
